subject: Trace/header scrubbing: scope, sample artifacts, and next ops
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Nguyen <lisa@careco.com>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — request/response logs & header masking (scope questions)

Hi Lisa — great to meet this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and the specific follow-ups you asked us to capture: 

1) Primary ask: CareCo wants assurance that sensitive identifiers (PHI-adjacent IDs, session tokens, trace IDs) do not appear in plaintext in our request/response logs or exported audit streams.
2) Retention constraint: you indicated billing/audit exports may need multi-year retention, but request/response logs used for debugging should be shorter-lived. You mentioned 90 days as a starting point.
3) Evidence: security team wants a concrete example of our redaction pipeline and a candidate retention table for each log class.

Attached: redaction-rules-draft.pdf — a first-pass mapping of log classes (ingest, request/response, access logs, audit exports) to redaction actions (hash, truncate, strip headers).

My suggested next steps: 
- We produce a short samples bundle (sanitized) showing before/after request logs with header-level masking and trace-id hashing.
- Define retention windows per log class (prod debug logs 90d masked, audit exports 7y aggregated, billing CSVs 7y).
- Small POC: enable header scrubbing + trace-id salt hashing in a dedicated sandbox for CareCo and share the sanitized export.

Can you confirm that 90 days for debug/logs and 7 years for audit/billing is the right starting point? Also confirm who on security should get the sample bundle (I can send to Mike if that works).

Thanks — will loop Marissa and Sean to align on the POC timeline.

—Kimberly Park
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redaction-rules-draft.pdf (12 pages, PDF)

From: Lisa Nguyen <lisa@careco.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Patel <security@careco.com>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — request/response logs & header masking (scope questions)

Kimberly — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming a few points from our side: 

- 90 days retention for verbatim debug request/response logs is acceptable only if those logs are redacted such that any PHI or persistent identifiers (patient_id, ssn fields, full trace IDs) are either removed or irreversibly transformed (hashing with a per-customer salt).
- Audit exports used for compliance (billing reconciliation, legal hold) must be retained for 7 years. Those can be an aggregated export — they should not contain full request/response payloads.
- Security would like an explicit statement about trace IDs: we need to know whether the trace ID is necessary for debugging across services (we use cross-service tracing) and if so, whether Redwood will support salted hashing at ingestion so the token cannot be re-associated externally.

Attaching the SOC2 / security questionnaire excerpt with the logging section highlighted. I've cc'd Mike — he will handle the evidence requests.

Lisa
Principal Product Manager, Integrations
CareCo Health
Attachments: socr-questions.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Nguyen <lisa@careco.com>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap — scope + next ops (CareCo)

Marissa / Sean — forwarding Lisa's reply. Action items I propose: 

- Marissa: can your infra team build a sanitized sample bundle (2 request/response pairs from sandbox + header set) where we show three redaction approaches: strip, regex mask, and hash-with-salt (salt not included in sample)? We should include the sanitized and original examples side-by-side in a spreadsheet (redacted fields only).
- Sean: confirm whether Redwood supports per-customer salt hashing at ingestion today or whether that requires a minor runtime change. If it’s not supported, estimate dev effort and whether Dedicated / Private deployments make this simpler.
- Kimberley: I'll draft a short one-pager mapping log class -> retention -> redaction action for review by CareCo security.

Also flagged: Lisa specifically asked whether trace IDs are necessary for cross-service debugging. If we offer to hash trace IDs (non-reversible), they will accept that for any logs shipped out of the VPC. That suggests our plan: hash at collection boundary, keep raw in ephemeral KV cache for 2 hours only, and never persist raw trace IDs to long-term logs.

Planned deliverables by EOD Friday: sample bundle + draft one-pager. Lisa / Mike — is Friday EOB (your timezone) OK for an initial package?

—Kim

On Tue, May 15, 2028 at 11:30 AM Lisa Nguyen <lisa@careco.com> wrote:
> Kimberly — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming a few points from our side: ...

From: Mike Patel <security@careco.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 May 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — request/response logs & header masking (scope questions)

Kimberly — thanks for the recap and the proposed plan. A few clarifications from security to make the evidence request precise: 

1) Trace IDs: acceptable if they are hashed with a per-customer salt at ingestion and the salt is managed in our KMS/HSM. Hashing must be one-way; we cannot accept reversible transformations.
2) Retention: audit/billing exports = 7 years (aggregated, no verbatim payloads). Debug request/response logs = 90 days maximum when persisted, but if raw request payloads are ever written to long-term storage they must be encrypted and access-controlled; masked copies are preferred.
3) Sample evidence we want: a sanitized sample log export (CSV) showing header scrubbing rules applied, a short diagram of the ingestion path showing where hashing happens, and a SOC2 control mapping referencing which control covers logging retention and access.

We can take the sample bundle Friday — please send to security@careco.com and I'll route internally. Also include the proposed retention table in the body of the email.

One more ask: can you include a short note about how Redwood distinguishes "audit export" vs "debug logs" so we can map to our retention policies? For example: audit export = aggregated events produced by scheduled job; debug logs = high-volume request/response telemetry.

Mike Patel
Security Architect, CareCo Health
